snippet.title: Clayface | Official Trailer
snippet.description:
Meet the new face of Gotham. #ClayfaceMovie only in theaters October 23.

DC Studios’ “Clayface” is a horror thriller from director James Watkins, starring Tom Rhys Harries in the title role of the cult favorite villain from Gotham’s rogues gallery.

Matt Hagen’s meteoric rise from Gotham street kid to Hollywood leading man is tragically cut short when a local crime boss’s actions leave him horribly disfigured. Abandoned by his team and with nothing left, Matt seeks out a cutting edge treatment that miraculously returns him to his former self… but also unexpectedly affects his grip on reality, spiraling him down a destructive path of all-consuming revenge.

The film also stars Naomi Ackie, David Dencik, Max Minghella and Eddie Marsan, as well as Nancy Carroll and Joshua James.

James Watkins directs from a screenplay by Mike Flanagan and Hossein Amini, story by Flanagan, based on characters from DC. The film is produced by Matt Reeves, Lynn Harris, James Gunn and Peter Safran, with Michael E. Uslan, Chantal Nong Vo, Lars P. Winther, Rafi Crohn and Paul Ritchie executive producing.

Watkins’ creative team includes director of photography Rob Hardy, production designer James Price, editor Jon Harris and costume designer Keith Madden. Music is by Volker Bertelmann.

DC Studios Presents a 6th & Idaho Production, a James Watkins Film, “Clayface.” The film will be distributed by Warner Bros. Pictures and released only in theaters in North America on October 23, 2026, and internationally beginning 21 October 2026.

snippet.title: Mtemi Afrika - STREET CODE (ft Mtalibani Halisi) Official Music Video
snippet.description:
Published on July 24, 2026, STREET CODE is another coastal affair in which Mtemi Afrika from VOI 
(Vilimani) teams up with Mtalibani Halisi from MOMBASA (Shamba) to create a mantric street ballard. The hardcore lyrics outline the daily struggles of an ordinary kenyan, mostly with a low income, how they work relentlessly hard to make ends meet, and how satisfying it is to put something on the table at the end of the day. Coupled with the memory-friendly melodies, the song puts special emphasis on taking responsibility and being independent. A coastal town and a coastal city in Kenya brought together by art.

"Nawapa Mgongo" is a powerful Swahili song that encourages people to mind their own business, work hard, and avoid gossip, envy, and unnecessary interference in other people's lives. Inspired by 1 Thessalonians 4:11 and 2 Thessalonians 3:11, the song reminds listeners that true peace comes from focusing on their own purpose instead of judging others. Let the talk continue as you keep moving forward.

1.
Nawapa mgongo, mseme mchoke, Juu kulala mtalala usiku, Keshoye mkaamke na njaa. Mambo ya kwangu hayashibishi, Peni na ndururu pia havikupi. Jipe shughuli, wachana na mimi.

Chorus
Wewe wa kusema sema, Wengine hakijakupata tu. Na hata wa kutenda tenda mabaya, Hujatendewa tu.
Chuma chako ki motoni, Jifunze kuwa mtulivu. Mambo ya wengine yakuhusia nini? Pilipili usiyoila yakuwashia ni?
Mwenzako akinyolewa, Chako kitie maji.

(1 Wathesalonike 4:11)
Mjitahidi kutulia, na kutenda shughuli zenu.

Twasikia kwamba wako waendao bila utaratibu, hawana shughuli zao wenyewe, wanajishughulisha na ya wengine.
